main_text.l: confugiunt ad potentes viros, vt si per infci-
tiam non possunt, vincant per personam.
2 Sed quid respondet Christus? Negat Mo-
ses mandasse: sed permisisse tantum, idque
ob singularem duritiem cordis eorum, vitan-
di nempe maioris mali causa, ne forte interfi-
cerent uxores, vt Hieronymus exponit, aut in
coniugio scortarentur: sed Deum creatorem
a principio non sic ordinasse, cuius ordina-
tio perpetuo valere debeat. Moses, inquit, πρὸς
τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν (quam Moses ipse,
Israeli non semel exprobrauit, nominatim ve-
ro Deuter. 9. & 31.) permisit (non praecepit,
quasi Deo probaretur, aut natura rectum es-
set: neque enim is probat diuortium, qui hoc
maluit admitti, quam homicidium) vobis re-
pudiare uxores vestras: caeterum ab initio
non fuit sic: quum scilicet nondum increuis-
set hominum malitia: neque nunc relaxabi-
tur idem ius, postea quam euangelica doctri-
na renouat ac perficit naturae synceritatem.
Sequitur enim in responsione Christi, Dico
autem vobis, quod quicunque repudiauerit
uxorem suam, nisi ob stuprum (mulier enim
scortando se quasi putridum membrum a vi-
ro resecindens, eum liberat, vñ bricht die ehe,)
& aliam duxerit, is committit adulterium.
Et qui repudiatam duxerit, is adulterium
committit. Quanquam haec verba (quibus
Christus indicat, quatenus liceat dimittere,
aut non) Marcus cap. 10. seorsum discipu-
lis suis fuisse dicta refert, quum domum venissent.

page.notes: Greek phrase "πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν" is printed in Greek; the first word is hard to make out at the scan resolution and is marked as printed-looking, not verified. The German words in black letter ("vñ bricht die ehe") are uncertain and may read differently. The word "infci-tiam" at the line break is uncertain. The page number "190" at top left is uncertain. Long s has been written as plain s throughout; the printed "Mofes", "Christi", "sic" etc. are read as Moses, Christi, sic. The catchword "sent." is the start of the next page's word split across the line break.
